functions.name: ComputeSprungMasses
functions.signature: ComputeSprungMasses(Mass Spring Positions, Total Mass, Out Sprung Masses)
functions.docs:
Compute the distribution of the mass of a body among springs.
This method assumes that spring positions are given relative
to the center of mass of the body, and that gravity occurs
in the local -Z direction.
Returns true if it was able to find a valid mass configuration.
If only one or two springs are included, then a valid
configuration may not result in a stable suspension system -
a bicycle or pogostick, for example, which is not perfectly centered
may have a valid sprung mass configuration without being stable.

functions.name: ComputeSprungMasses
functions.signature: ComputeSprungMasses(Local Spring Positions, Local Center Of Mass, Total Mass, Out Sprung Masses)
functions.docs:
Same as above, but allows the caller to specify spring locations
in a local space which is not necessarily originated at the center
of mass.

functions.name: ComputeNaturalFrequency
functions.docs: Natural frequency of spring in radians/sec - divide by 2Pi to get result in Hz

functions.name: ComputeCriticalDamping
functions.docs: Compute spring damping value that will achieve critical damping

functions.name: ComputeDamping
functions.signature: ComputeDamping(Spring Rate, Sprung Mass, Damping Ratio)
functions.docs: Compute spring damping value that will achieve the desired damping ratio. A damping ratio between 0.2-0.5 is typical of vehicle suspension
